gaps.sentence: "I will call you tomorrow." — She said she ___ me the next day.
"Where do you live?" — He asked me where I ___.
'She arrived last night,' he told us. He told us that she had arrived ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Last night' becomes the night before (the previous night) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you seen my reading glasses?' he asked. He asked ___ his reading glasses.
gaps.explanation: 'If/whether' reports a yes/no question; the tense backshifts to past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'We'd already booked when you called,' they said. They said they ___ already booked when I called.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect stays past perfect; only the pronoun you → I shifts.

gaps.sentence: 'They were arguing all through dinner,' he said. He said they ___ arguing all through dinner.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: were arguing → had been arguing.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you finished the report?' the boss asked. The boss asked ___ finished the report.
gaps.hint: present perfect → past perfect in a yes/no question
gaps.explanation: Have you finished → whether/if I had finished; statement word order throughout.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm sorry I shouted at you,' he said. He ___ shouting at me.
gaps.explanation: Apologies take apologise for + -ing: apologised for shouting.
